title: Gukesh Draws Game 2 in 20 Moves as World Title Match Stays Level
excerpt: The defending champion's London System was met by a prepared Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, and the second straight draw leaves the FIDE World Championship tied 1-1 with Game 3 on Thursday.
body:
• Game 2 of the FIDE World Championship in Geneva ended in a 20-move draw by repetition on Wednesday, leaving champion Gukesh Dommaraju and challenger Javokhir Sindarov level at 1-1.
  • Gukesh, playing White, chose the London System, but Sindarov was well prepared and the game was agreed drawn just as a bold pawn push threatened to heat it up.
  • Both opening games have now been drawn; Game 1, with Sindarov as White, lasted 38 moves in a Ruy Lopez.
  • Game 3 is on Thursday, November 26, at 3:00 p.m. Geneva time (7:30 p.m. IST), with Sindarov playing White. The first player to 7.5 points in the 14-game match takes the title.

Defending champion Gukesh Dommaraju's first game with the white pieces at the Salesforce FIDE World Championship 2026 lasted just 20 moves, as challenger Javokhir Sindarov held a comfortable draw by repetition in Geneva on Wednesday to keep the match level at 1-1.

Gukesh opened with the London System, a solid setup that gives White a risk-free structure, but Sindarov was ready for it. According to Chess.com's report, Gukesh once again fell behind on the clock, and just when Sindarov had played a bold pawn push and the position seemed about to sharpen, the players repeated moves and the game ended.

"The prize fund is $2.5 million, with $200,000 paid for each game won and the remaining money split equally."

How the draw unfolded

ChessBase India recorded the closing sequence: Gukesh played 17.Be5, Sindarov replied 17...Nd7, and after 18.Bg3 Nf6 and 19.Be5 Nd7 the position repeated and the point was split. ChessBase India noted Gukesh was trailing Sindarov by around 40 minutes on the clock when he chose to repeat moves — a pragmatic decision with Black's position fully sound, securing Sindarov a comfortable half-point with the black pieces.

The result follows the same pattern as Game 1 on Tuesday, when Sindarov, playing White, pressed in a Ruy Lopez but Gukesh held the draw in 38 moves. Two games in, neither player has yet landed a blow, and the higher-rated player in the match so far is the challenger: Sindarov is rated 2782 to Gukesh's 2710.

The match in numbers

The match in Geneva runs from November 24 to December 12 and is played over a maximum of 14 classical games, with the winner the first to reach 7.5 points. The time control is two hours for the first 40 moves, then 30 minutes to finish, with a 30-second increment per move from move 41. The prize fund is $2.5 million, with $200,000 paid for each game won and the remaining money split equally. If the match is tied 7-7, a playoff begins with four games of 15+10 rapid chess.

What is next

Game 3 is played on Thursday, November 26, starting at 3:00 p.m. in Geneva — 9:00 a.m. ET and 7:30 p.m. IST — with Sindarov holding the white pieces for the second time in the match, before the first rest day. Live coverage with commentary is carried on ChessBase's live page and FIDE's broadcast. With 12 games still to play, the opening question of the match is unchanged: whether Gukesh can create winning chances with White more ambitious than a 20-move London System draw, and whether Sindarov's rating edge and preparation keep neutralising him.
